LESSON MMXM · MMXM

Market Maker Model (MMXM)

A broad campaign narrative describing price moving away from an origin range in stages, reaching a higher-timeframe reference area, and potentially reversing through prior ranges or pauses. The wording does not prove the actual orders or intentions of a market maker.

CANONICAL NAME / ALIASES

Market Maker Model (MMXM) · Market Maker Model · MMXM

SOURCE / EVIDENCE LABELCONVENTION · PERFORMANCE: NO DATA

This term is supplemental or convention-sensitive in the supplied catalogue. Do not treat it as a universal/core ICT definition. Keep source variants separate and do not use it operationally until the exact definition is pinned to a primary source.

CONCEPT IDENTITY

Definition and purpose

A broad campaign narrative describing price moving away from an origin range in stages, reaching a higher-timeframe reference area, and potentially reversing through prior ranges or pauses. The wording does not prove the actual orders or intentions of a market maker.

04

IDENTIFICATION RULES

How to identify the concept

  1. Mark the original consolidation or dealing range.
  2. Map the first directional leg and intermediate consolidations as price moves away from the origin.
  3. Identify a higher-timeframe reference area where a reversal would need separate confirmation.
  4. Only map the next leg after a clear structure/delivery shift; mark invalidation and opposing liquidity.

ENTRY AND ORDER ASSUMPTIONS

Execution study — no live orders

NOT AN ENTRY SIGNAL

Require the preconditions and invalidation rules before recording an entry hypothesis.

  • Entry examples are replay assumptions, not live execution.
  • Limit, stop and market orders have different fill/slippage behaviour; record the assumption.
  • The Academy does not route or execute orders.
10

STOP PLACEMENT AND SIZING

Risk is calculated from the verified contract

No fixed tick stop is supplied by this concept. A hypothetical stop belongs beyond the level/structure that invalidates the setup; convert to money risk using current tick value and stop ticks.

Show commission, exchange/clearing fees and slippage separately.

See Contract Specs & Tick Math and Futures Margin & Position Risk. Risk & position sizing →

11

TARGETS AND PARTIAL MANAGEMENT

Example management only

No target is promised. If the chosen model specifies one, pre-mark the relevant opposing level and record the partial/runner rule as a test assumption.

Example only; not a guaranteed result or performance statistic.

12

INVALIDATION RULES

What disproves the study

  1. The predeclared identification rule is not met or the specified close/wick condition contradicts it.
  2. The swing, reference level, session or source cannot be reproduced.
  3. An expiry mismatch, stale feed or continuous-series splice invalidates the comparison.
13

NO-TRADE CONDITIONS

Common failures and no-trade rules

  1. Retrofitting every chart into a buy/sell campaign; treating “market maker” language as evidence of a specific institution; assuming the entire path must complete.
  2. A sweep, time window or isolated zone is not an entry by itself.
  3. Do not rely on stale specs, unknown roll mappings or unavailable source data.
14

DEFINITION VARIANTS

Conflicting sources and terminology

  1. Record wick-versus-close, body-versus-wick, pivot-lookback and mitigation variants where applicable.
  2. Retain conflicting source definitions with source URLs rather than silently choosing one.
  3. Community conventions are not universal exchange rules.

PRACTICE TASK

Chart replay and written deliverable

Chart-replay assignment

Replay five completed sessions with America/New_York selected. Record the exact window, exchange schedule and DST-aware IST conversion.

Save / submit

A dated screenshot or chart pack plus a short rule sheet. The work is considered complete when a second person can reproduce the classification from the recorded rules.

Review criteria

  • The rule was written before outcome review.
  • The chart evidence matches the rule and includes timestamp/timeframe.
  • Invalidation and disqualified cases are documented.
